# hunch init: examples

`init` writes the config, and the Actions workflow when asked. At a terminal it asks with arrow keys; any flag skips the questions, which is how an agent runs it.

<!-- case: init-yes -->
### Take the detected defaults

A `package.json` means TypeScript: `hunch.config.ts` with the recommended and TypeScript presets.

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch init --yes
```

Exit code **0**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: wrote hunch.config.ts.
```

`hunch.config.ts` afterwards:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@kelbie/hunch";

export default defineConfig({
  extends: ["hunch:recommended", "hunch:typescript"],
  include: ["**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}"],
  ignore: ["dist/**", "node_modules/**", "**/*.generated.ts", "hunch.config.ts"],
});
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: init-rust -->
### A Rust crate gets TOML

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch init --yes
```

Exit code **0**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: wrote hunch.toml.
```

`hunch.toml` afterwards:

```toml
extends = ["hunch:recommended", "hunch:rust"]
include = ["**/*.rs"]
ignore = ["target/**"]
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: init-everything -->
### Every answer as a flag

A mixed repository, reviewed by the GitHub App, on Vercel Hobby, with one rule of its own.

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch init --preset ts,rust --target app --include "src/**" --no-zero-data-retention --fail-on-error --rule api/stable-errors="Error responses keep their code field, because clients branch on it."
```

Exit code **0**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: wrote hunch.config.ts.

Next:

1. Install the App on this repository:
   https://github.com/apps/hunch-review/installations/new

2. Commit to your default branch:
   git add hunch.config.ts
   git commit -m "Review PRs with Hunch"
   git push

3. Open a PR. Hunch reads its rules from the base branch, so the PR that adds Hunch is skipped — that is expected.

No review? Run: npx @kelbie/hunch doctor
```

`hunch.config.ts` afterwards:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@kelbie/hunch";

export default defineConfig({
  extends: ["hunch:recommended", "hunch:typescript", "hunch:rust"],
  include: ["src/**"],
  ignore: ["dist/**", "node_modules/**", "**/*.generated.ts", "hunch.config.ts", "target/**"],
  failOnError: true,
  // Vercel Hobby cannot enforce zero data retention; see the Hunch skill's config reference.
  zeroDataRetention: false,
  rules: {
    "api/stable-errors": ["warn", "Error responses keep their code field, because clients branch on it."],
  },
});
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: init-actions -->
### Review PRs with GitHub Actions

Writes the workflow as well. It pins the Action to the version that wrote it.

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch init --preset general --target actions
```

Exit code **0**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: wrote hunch.toml.
hunch: wrote .github/workflows/hunch.yml.

Next:

1. Set the model key as a repository secret:
   gh secret set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY

2. Commit both files to your default branch:
   git add hunch.toml .github/workflows/hunch.yml
   git commit -m "Review PRs with Hunch"
   git push

3. Open a PR. The review appears under Checks → Hunch. The PR that adds Hunch is skipped — that is expected.
```

`hunch.toml` afterwards:

```toml
extends = ["hunch:recommended"]
ignore = ["node_modules/**", "dist/**", "target/**", ".git/**"]
```

`.github/workflows/hunch.yml` afterwards:

```yaml
name: Hunch
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, edited]
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: hunch-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  review:
    if: >-
      !github.event.pull_request.draft &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check API key setup
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo '::error::Add AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY in Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions.'
            exit 1
          fi
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: Kelbie/hunch@v0.21.0
        with:
          base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          head: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
```

<!-- /case -->

<!-- case: init-exists -->
### A config already exists

init never rewrites a config. Edit the file instead, then run `hunch config`.

```sh
npx -y --min-release-age=0 @kelbie/hunch init --yes
```

Exit code **2**.

stderr:

```text
hunch: a hunch config already exists. Edit it, or use `npx @kelbie/hunch init --target actions` to add only the workflow.
```

<!-- /case -->
